chunks: From him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yazid and Yunus ibn Dhabyan, who said:

We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who enters into ihram in the month of Rajab or in the month of Ramadan, so when the time for Hajj arrives, he performs Hajj al-Tamattu'. He said: 'There is no harm in that.' And we have fully covered what relates to this chapter in our Great Book, and what we have mentioned is sufficient, if God wills.

key_terms.رَجَبٍ: the seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately)
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters into the state of ritual consecration (ihram)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to enter ihram in Ramadan and perform Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirmed the permissibility of entering the state of ihram during Rajab or Ramadan to perform Hajj al-Tamattu' when the Hajj season arrives, a ruling that underscores the flexibility of ritual timing in Shia jurisprudence. This narration, cited by Shaykh al-Tusi in al-Istibsar, serves as a concise confirmation of the broader legal principles detailed in al-Kulayni’s al-Kafi, highlighting the scholarly tradition of cross-referencing major hadith collections for comprehensive legal coverage.
